name: too-new-by-signing-key
why: A signing key cannot make an identity too new, or a thief could hide it from every copy.

name: too-new-by-retired-key
why: A retired signing key cannot do it either.

name: too-new-by-recovery-key
why: A recovery key on the identity's tree can, including the next one, which no succession has used yet.

name: duplicate-other-author
why: A record with another author's dedupe ref does not make that author's record a duplicate, whatever the ids.

name: duplicate-same-author
why: Two records of one author with one ref are duplicates. The lowest id is the primary.

name: checkpoint-missing
why: A record that a checkpoint covers must be in the set.

name: checkpoint-and-tombstone
why: A valid tombstone of the identity explains a covered record that is gone.

name: checkpoint-stranger-tombstone
why: Another identity's tombstone does not explain it.

name: retired-claim-unattested
why: A claim of a retired key that nothing vouches for stays valid but is unattested.

name: retired-claim-sealed
why: The succession that ended the key can vouch for the claim.

name: retired-claim-covered-by-later-key
why: A checkpoint of a later key can vouch for the claim.

name: retired-checkpoint-unsealed
why: A checkpoint of a retired key needs a seal, like a deletion, so a thief's checkpoint does not vouch for a thief's claim.

name: stranger-checkpoint-does-not-attest
why: A checkpoint of another identity vouches for nothing.

name: freeze-sealed-by-both
why: A correction by the key at a fork stays valid when both branches sealed it.

name: freeze-sealed-by-one
why: It does not when only one branch sealed it, so neither party decides alone.

name: freeze-claim-by-fork-key
why: A claim by the key at a fork stays valid, but is unattested unless every branch sealed it. A thief can still write with that key.

name: missing-named-by-two-identities
why: Two identities that name one missing id each get a line. The result does not depend on map order.

name: held-succession-not-valid
why: A succession not on the tree is held and not valid. Its signature proves nothing, because no key was checked.

name: unattested-copy-of-ref
why: An unattested claim is not in a duplicate group, so a retired key cannot hide a record by copying its ref.

name: tombstone-of-checkpoint
why: A tombstone must not name a checkpoint.
